assertion_audit.fails_if: The code rewrites index.json on a reconcile that changed no entry, so the inode, mtime and size tuple differs; shown red in logs/negative-control.log.
An unchanged reconcile writes different bytes to the document.
A freshly started process must list the store; the probe records scandir. logs/repro-base-second-process-lists-once.log shows the instrument seeing a listing at base.
The cold process answers a document holding fewer than 32 entries.
A record the test wrote is masked by the stamp and never reaches the document.
Adding a record leaves the document's bytes untouched.

assertion_independence: No added assertion compares a value the test supplied against the same value returned. The document's stat and bytes are read from the filesystem on both sides, and the listing count comes from a separate interpreter that patches os.scandir and Path.glob before importing the module. The entry-count and added-record assertions use values the test wrote, but each can redden on a code change (an empty answer, or a masked record).

findings.text: blocking: the autouse fixture calls review_records._SETTLED_IDENTITIES, which this change deletes. A tree at the reviewed head runs this file as 2 errors at setup where base runs 2 passed, so promoting this change alone reddens the primary branch. The one-line fixture deletion must land with it; the node reported it under outside_scope.

non-blocking: _read_index_stamp wraps json.loads in its own except clause, re-implementing read_cache_document at review_records.py:1356, whose docstring forbids exactly that. Call the owner and validate its result.

non-blocking: _persist_index_stamp re-implements write_cache_document at review_records.py:1371 and omits its fsync=False and mode=None cache flags, so each settled-identity advance fsyncs a cache file and is created 0600, unlike the document write at line 2127 whose docstring the helper claims to mirror.

justifications.durability: tests/test_an_unchanged_reconcile_writes_only_its_stamp.py:180-187 fails when the document is rewritten and :191-195 fails when a cold process lists the store, and logs/negative-control.log shows it firing on the declared mutation.
justifications.evidence: logs/arm-base.log and logs/arm-head.log both cover the same three files and neither includes tests/test_a_review_index_reader_never_waits_or_rewrites.py, so the done_when's no-failure-against-base clause was measured without the file this change breaks.
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/review_records.py:1938-2006 follows the module's private-helper and cache-write idiom and carries no plan or ticket label, but the stamp writer's call omits the fsync and mode flags the document write beside it passes.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/review_records.py:1938-2006 stores the settled identity in .review-index/stamp.json and leaves the document untouched when a reconcile changes no entry, which is what the goal asks for.
justifications.reuse: reckon/crew/review_records.py:1950-1995 re-implements read_cache_document (line 1356) and write_cache_document (line 1371), the module's own owners of this cache-read and cache-write capability.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff at d89c36e124 touches only the three granted paths, and the file it breaks outside that grant is reported under outside_scope rather than edited.

recommendation: Repair the blocking finding first: delete the dead fresh_settled_identities fixture (one line) so the importing test file runs green at the head, then land. The two non-blocking findings are cleanup the stamp helpers should fold into the existing cache-document owners.
